items.title: Dave Brubeck — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Charles Ives have used the jazz idiom.

ctx.x: Taylor has said, “This is America’s classical music.” This we got to realize, that it’s the basic music of every Broadway show you go to, of rock, of movies – especially in a chase scene. It’s always jazz. Our classical composers that are world-wide known – and this is what Darius Milhaud told me – if you want to express, you have to use the jazz idiom, just as Bartok used the Hungarian folk music, and I’ve used French music, and Bach – Bach used drinking songs. O Sacred Head Now Wounded is a drinking song. Why…

Dave, I think I interviewed you back in 1988. At that time I had found an interview you had given in the 1950s in which you had told an interviewer that you would like to spend more time doing classical composition. I mentioned that to you in this 1988 interview, and you said, “I still feel the same way today. I wish I was spending more time doing classical composition.” It seems to me, though, that you have – in the last 20 years, you’ve devoted increasing amounts of time to these compositions.
